extracted.intended_audience: authors, journal editors, peer reviewers, and journal staff working in medical/biomedical journals
extracted.subtask_description: The ICMJE Recommendations provide standards and guidance for the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals, covering roles/responsibilities, authorship, conflicts of interest, peer review, trial registration, manuscript preparation, and other editorial and ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Recommendations — their purpose for guiding the conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page lists this section title only; full explanatory guidance is contained in the ICMJE Recommendations (see downloadable PDF, updated April 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Intended users of the Recommendations (who should apply these standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigation-only on this archived page; consult full Recommendations for specifics about roles and responsibilities for authors, editors, publishers, and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles & Responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Broad standards for roles and responsibilities of parties involved in scholarly publishing (authors, editors, reviewers, publishers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present; detailed responsibilities and expectations are in the full Recommendations document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and definitions for who qualifies as an author or contributor and what their responsibilities are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the section heading appears here; full text includes authorship criteria, contributor roles, and expectations for accountability (see PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for declaring financial and non-financial relationships, activities, and conflicts of interest by authors (and others where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title is listed; the detailed form and instructions (disclosure expectations, timing, examples) are in the Recommendations and associated disclosure forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations and standards for conduct during manuscript submission and peer review (for authors, reviewers, and editors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only on this page; the full Recommendations elaborate on confidentiality, timeliness, reviewer selection, and handling of conflicts during peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on the relationship between journal owners/publishers and editorial independence/freedom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only present as a label here; full guidance addresses protecting editorial decisions from owner/publisher interference and transparency about ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards to protect human (and other) research participants, including consent and ethical approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section listed; the Recommendations contain substantive requirements about ethics committee approval, informed consent, privacy, and reporting of protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing & Editorial Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: General editorial and publishing issues impacting integrity, quality, and transparency of published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only; see full Recommendations for specifics such as editorial policies, peer-review models, and editorial workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for issuing corrections, retractions, expressions of concern, and maintaining version control of published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a section title; detailed processes and criteria for corrections and retractions are in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and definitions related to scientific misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) and how journals should respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the title appears here; the Recommendations give definitions, investigative responsibilities, and recommended responses in the full document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on copyright ownership, licensing, and transfer related to published works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section heading only; consult the full Recommendations for recommended practices on copyright and licensing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards regarding duplicate submission, redundant publication, and overlapping publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading appears without detail here; full Recommendations describe acceptable overlap, disclosure, and how journals should handle redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and expectations for letters to the editor, author responses, and post-publication correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title present; full guidance addresses handling, publication, and responses to correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies regarding fees charged to authors or readers (e.g., article processing charges, page charges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a heading; full Recommendations include disclosure and transparency expectations about fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for publishing supplements, themed issues, or special series, including sponsorship and editorial control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only here; the full document outlines transparency, peer review, and disclosure requirements for supplements and sponsored content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on relationships between journals and sponsors or partners and related disclosure/independence issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present; full Recommendations provide expectations for disclosure and protection of editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards related to online publishing practices, electronic archiving, metadata, and accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a section; the detailed Recommendations cover electronic formats, archiving, identifiers (DOIs), and online corrections/versioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing advertising in journals and separation of advertising from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only here; the Recommendations address boundaries between advertising and editorial influence and required disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interactions between journals/authors and the media, including press releases and embargoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title present; consult full Recommendations for detailed guidance on media handling and accurate communication of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for clinical trial reporting, registration, and transparent reporting of methods and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section heading only on this archived page; the full Recommendations include registration requirements, CONSORT adherence, and result-reporting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials Registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement/expectation that clinical trials be registered in a publicly accessible registry prior to enrollment of the first participant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in navigation; full Recommendations specify acceptable registries, minimum registration data, and consequences for unregistered trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Preparation and Submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for preparing manuscripts for submission to medical journals, including formatting, structure, and required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section title present; the Recommendations provide detailed instructions on title pages, abstracts, structured reporting, ethical statements, and supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical instructions and requirements authors must follow when preparing manuscripts for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading repeated in navigation; detailed content (e.g., reporting guidelines, author declarations) is in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Manuscript to the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and expectations when submitting a manuscript (cover letters, declarations, submission systems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigation-only here; full text covers submission checklists, required disclosures, and handling of simultaneous submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on publishing translations of articles, including permissions and disclosure of original publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the section heading appears; detailed expectations for translations are in the complete Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archives
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for archiving published content for long-term access and preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heading only; full Recommendations discuss archiving policies, repositories, and responsibilities for maintaining access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Interest / Disclosure Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms and forms for declaring interests, including financial and non-financial disclosures; associated documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both 'Disclosure of Interest' and 'Disclosure Forms' are listed; the full Recommendations and downloadable forms contain the required wording, timing, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Resources (FAQs, Membership, News & Editorials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ancillary resources including FAQs, membership information, news/editorials, and other miscellaneous materials supporting the Recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present as navigation items; useful background but not substantive standards themselves. Full resources available from ICMJE website and PDFs.
